subject: Vocabulary
topic: One-Word Substitution — Phobias, Manias, Social Roles and Science Terms (W13 B1)

questions.stem: An irrational and extreme fear of heights is called:
questions.explanation: C is correct. ACROPHOBIA = extreme or irrational fear of heights (Greek akron = highest point + phobia = fear). Trap: hydrophobia = fear of water; claustrophobia = fear of enclosed/confined spaces (claustrum = enclosed place); agoraphobia = fear of open or crowded places (agora = marketplace). Must-know phobia set for SSC: acro(heights), hydro(water), claustro(confined), agora(open/crowd), xeno(strangers), pyro(fire), necro(death), aero(flying).

questions.stem: A person with an obsessive passion for setting fires is called a:
questions.explanation: B is correct. PYROMANIAC = a person with an irresistible urge to start fires (Greek pyr = fire + mania = obsession). Mania = obsessive compulsion. Trap: kleptomaniac = obsessive stealing (Greek kleptein = to steal); egomaniac = obsessive self-importance; misanthrope = hater of humankind (not a mania). SSC loves the -mania set: pyromania(fire), kleptomania(stealing), megalomania(power), bibliomania(books), monomania(single idea).

questions.stem: A person who can use both hands equally well is called:
questions.explanation: C is correct. AMBIDEXTROUS = able to use both hands with equal skill (Latin ambi = both + dexter = right hand). Both hands are as capable as the right. Trap: ambivalent = having mixed feelings (ambi = both + valent = strong, but applied to feelings not hands); dexterous = skilled with the right hand; sinistral = left-handed (Latin sinister = left). Classic SSC one-word substitution.

questions.stem: A system of government where the highest power is held by an extremely small, elite group is called:
questions.explanation: C is correct. OLIGARCHY = a small group of people controlling a country or organisation (Greek oligos = few + archein = to rule). Trap: democracy = rule by the people; theocracy = rule by divine authority or priests; autocracy = rule by a single person with unlimited power. All end in -cracy/-archy (rule). SSC loves this -archy/-cracy set: monar(one), oligar(few), pluto(wealthy), techno(experts), ochlo(mob), demo(people).

questions.stem: An expert who appraises and authenticates works of art is called a:
questions.explanation: A is correct. CONNOISSEUR = an expert judge in matters of taste; a person with deep knowledge and refined appreciation of the fine arts, food or wine. Trap: bibliophile = lover of books (bibliophilia); philanthropist = one who helps others (love of humanity); iconoclast = one who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions (literally: breaker of icons). Connoisseur comes from French connaître = to know well.

questions.stem: A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially at their funeral, is called a:
questions.explanation: C is correct. EULOGY = a speech or written tribute that praises a person, especially one delivered at their funeral (Greek eu = well + logos = speech). Trap: epitaph = inscription on a grave/tombstone (not a spoken tribute — it's written on stone); elegy = a mournful poem lamenting someone's death (not always a praise speech); epigram = a short, witty saying. E-words cluster: eulogy (spoken praise), epitaph (gravestone text), elegy (mournful poem), epic (long heroic poem).

questions.stem: An inscription on a coin or medal is called a:
questions.explanation: A is correct. LEGEND (numismatic sense) = the inscription on a coin or medal, typically giving the name of the issuing authority, denomination, or commemorative details. (Also: legend = a traditional story, a key on a map.) Trap: motto = a short phrase expressing values (on shields, flags, not specifically coins); caption = text accompanying an image (not specific to coins); epigraph = inscription at start of a book or on a building. The LEGEND on a coin is a frequently tested SSC one-word substitution.

questions.stem: A person who is fanatically devoted to a single cause or idea to the exclusion of all else is called a:
questions.explanation: C is correct. MONOMANIAC = a person who is excessively or obsessively focused on a single subject or idea (Greek monos = single + mania = obsession). 'To the exclusion of all else' is the key phrase indicating monomania. Trap: zealot = a fanatically devoted person (passionate, but not narrowly single-focused — could have multiple causes); sycophant = a flatterer who seeks favour (not related to single-cause devotion); chauvinist = exaggerated patriotism or belief in superiority (not general single-cause).

questions.stem: A place where animals are kept for public display and study is called a:
questions.explanation: D is correct. ZOOLOGICAL GARDEN (zoo) = a place where wild animals are kept for public display, study and conservation. Trap: aviary = enclosure specifically for birds; vivarium = enclosure for live animals (especially reptiles or small animals, not open to the general public for display); menagerie = a private or travelling collection of wild animals (less formal, not for scientific study). SSC tests these distinctions between similar-looking options.

questions.stem: A person who deliberately sets fire to buildings or property is called an:
questions.explanation: B is correct. ARSONIST = a person who deliberately and criminally sets fire to property (arson = the crime of deliberately setting fire to property). Key distinction from Q2: a PYROMANIAC is driven by an irresistible compulsion (mental disorder); an ARSONIST deliberately commits the crime (criminal intent). Trap: anarchist = one who advocates the abolition of all government; iconoclast = one who attacks traditional institutions. The arsonist/pyromaniac distinction is a favourite SSC nuance question.
